questions.explanation: The form "berebbero" is the conditional form for "loro" of "bere". Identifying the infinitive behind a conjugated form requires matching the stem and the person endings to the correct conjugation pattern.
questions.hint: Strip the ending and match the remaining stem to an infinitive.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.stem: In a grammar exercise, a language learner transcribes a single entry for practice. Choose the imperfect: "loro volere".

options.misconception: this is the voi form of the verb, not loro
this is the io form of the verb, not loro
this is the tu form of the verb, not loro

questions.explanation: The imperfect form of "volere" for "loro" is "volevano". The imperfect describes repeated or ongoing past actions. It is formed from the present stem with a characteristic set of endings. Selecting the wrong person ending changes who performs the action.
questions.hint: Identify the subject pronoun, then apply the imperfect ending for that person.
